title: HEAD and refs
summary: Branches and tags are names for commits, and HEAD is the name for where you are. Learn to point at any commit.

steps.title: Names for commits
body: Hashes are exact but unfriendly, so Git keeps **refs**: small files that hold a commit hash.
- A **branch** is a ref that moves forward automatically when you commit on it.
- A **tag** is a ref that stays put (module 4).
- **HEAD** is *you are here*. Usually it holds not a hash but the name of a branch: a **symbolic ref**. Committing moves the branch HEAD points to.
After `git commit`, a new commit D is made with parent C, and `main` moves to D. HEAD still says *main*.

steps.prompt: `.git/HEAD` contains `ref: refs/heads/feature`. You make a commit. What changes?
options: `refs/heads/feature` now holds the new commit's hash; `HEAD` still says `ref: refs/heads/feature`
`HEAD` now holds the new commit's hash directly
Both `main` and `feature` move to the new commit
steps.explain: Commit moves the branch that HEAD names. HEAD itself only changes when you switch branches (or detach it).

steps.title: Relative names: ~ and ^
body: You can count backwards from any name:
A <-- B <-- C <-- D   main, HEAD
| `HEAD^2` | **second** parent; only merge commits have one | - |
`~n` walks *n* generations along first parents. `^n` picks *which* parent of a merge. In daily life you mostly need `HEAD~n`.

steps.prompt: History is `A <-- B <-- C <-- D <-- E (main, HEAD)`. Which commit does each name point to? Answer with one letter per line, in order: `HEAD~2`, `main~4`, `HEAD^`, `main`.
steps.explain: `~2` is two steps back from E (D, then C). `main~4` walks back four to A. `^` is the first parent, D.

steps.prompt: Match each name to what it refers to.
pairs: the commit you have checked out right now
the tip of the main branch
the grandparent of the current commit
a fixed tag that never moves
the second parent of a merge commit

steps.prompt: Which of these names move on their own when you commit on `main`?
steps.explain: `main` gains the new commit, and `HEAD` and `HEAD~1` are relative to it. Tags, other branches and raw hashes are fixed.

steps.prompt: Complete the commands: show the commit two before HEAD, then print the full hash of the tip of `main`.
steps.explain: `git rev-parse` turns any name into a hash; scripts use it constantly.

steps.title: Resolve a revision
prompt: Model how Git turns a name into a commit. `refs` maps ref names to values; a value is either a commit id or `ref: <other ref>`. `parent` maps each commit to its first parent.
1. Split `rev` on `~`. The left part is a name; the right part (if present) is a step count. `X~` with nothing after means 1.
2. Look up the name: `HEAD` directly, otherwise `refs/heads/<name>`, otherwise `refs/tags/<name>`, otherwise treat it as a commit id.
3. While the value starts with `ref: `, follow it.
starter: static string Resolve(string rev, Dictionary<string, string> refs, Dictionary<string, string> parent)
solution: static string Resolve(string rev, Dictionary<string, string> refs, Dictionary<string, string> parent)
else if (refs.ContainsKey("refs/heads/" + name)) value = refs["refs/heads/" + name];
else if (refs.ContainsKey("refs/tags/" + name)) value = refs["refs/tags/" + name];
for (int i = 0; i < steps; i++) value = parent[value];
hints: `rev.Split('~')` gives one part (no tilde) or two.
Look up `HEAD` first, then `"refs/heads/" + name`, then `"refs/tags/" + name`.
template: var dojoRefs = new Dictionary<string, string> { ["HEAD"] = "ref: refs/heads/main", ["refs/heads/main"] = "D", ["refs/heads/feature"] = "F", ["refs/tags/v1"] = "B" };
Dojo.Eq("HEAD follows the symbolic ref", "D", Resolve("HEAD", dojoRefs, dojoPar));
Dojo.Eq("tag with ~ means one step", "A", Resolve("v1~", dojoRefs, dojoPar));
Dojo.Eq("raw commit id", "C", Resolve("C", dojoRefs, dojoPar));
